output.title: Dollar Threshold for Escalating Specialty Pharmacy Cases to the Pharmacy Director
output.draft_text:
Question: What dollar amount sends a specialty case to the pharmacy director?

Answer: A specialty pharmacy case must be escalated to the pharmacy director for review when the [cost measure, e.g., per-claim cost / monthly cost / annual projected cost] of the specialty medication meets or exceeds [dollar threshold amount].

How to apply the threshold:
1. Determine the [cost measure] for the case using [source system or document used to look up cost].
2. If the amount is [at or above / above] [dollar threshold amount], route the case to the pharmacy director using [escalation method, e.g., queue name, form, or contact].
3. Document the escalation in [case management system] with [required documentation fields].
4. Inform the member that the case is under additional review and that the expected review time is [number of business days].

Cases below the threshold: Cases below [dollar threshold amount] follow the standard specialty review process described in [reference to standard specialty review procedure].

Exceptions: [Any exceptions, e.g., urgent/expedited cases, specific drug classes, or plan types that follow a different threshold or path].

Effective date: This threshold is effective as of [effective date] and applies to [plans or lines of business covered].

author_checklist: Confirm the exact dollar threshold that triggers pharmacy director escalation and cite the source policy document.
Confirm which cost basis the threshold applies to (per claim, per fill, monthly, annual, or projected course of therapy).
Confirm whether the threshold is triggered at the amount ('at or above') or only when exceeded ('above').
Confirm where advocates find the cost figure for a case.
Confirm the escalation route (queue, form, contact) and required documentation.
Confirm the expected turnaround time for pharmacy director review and what advocates may tell members.
Confirm any exceptions for urgent cases, specific drug classes, or plan types.
Confirm the effective date and the plans or lines of business the threshold applies to.
Confirm the policy owner and review cadence so the threshold is updated if it changes.
Verify no conflicting threshold exists in other approved pharmacy or specialty documents.
